subject: Request: custom SLA addendum and order-form language for uptime/latency
messages:
From: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@nexushealthtech.com>
To: PrIyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@nexushealthtech.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: SLA addendum request — uptime/latency commitments

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the throughput and consistency on the dedicated cluster look promising. Our procurement and infra teams reviewed the draft MSA/SOW and flagged two items we need explicit order-form / addendum language for before we can proceed:

1) Availability commitment: we need a 99.5% monthly uptime commitment for the hosted endpoint backing our pilot, with clear measurement windows and credit calculations.
2) Latency SLO: P95 under 250ms for standard production routes (we understand tail behavior varies by model and region; happy to call out model variants).

Procurement attached the redlines to the MSA and the SOW (see attachments). We expect some carve-outs — planned maintenance, force majeure, and regional failovers — but need those defined explicitly (duration thresholds, notification windows, and what counts as a creditable outage).

Can Redwood propose concrete addendum language and the exact order-form phrasing your billing team needs to trigger credits? Also, please highlight any operational limitations (e.g., maintenance windows > 2 hours, backend model swaps) that would require SLA exceptions.

Goal: finalize SLA addendum + order form language this week so we can route to legal/procurement for signature.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Hayes
Head of Platform Operations | Nexus HealthTech
jordan.hayes@nexushealthtech.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: Nexus_MSA_Redlines_20261130.pdf, SOW_Draft_Nexus_v3.docx
From: PrIyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@nexushealthtech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-05T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA addendum request — uptime/latency commitments

Jordan — thanks for the clear asks and for sending the redlines. Looping in Marissa (account lead) and Laura (legal/order forms) to draft concrete language.

High-level response up front: we can support a 99.5% monthly availability SLA for the hosted API used in your pilot with an agreed set of carve-outs. For latency, we can commit to P95 <= 250ms for the primary region on our dedicated tier for production traffic; hosted multi-region routes can be a P95 objective with a different credit profile.

I'll propose specific addendum text below and attach a one-page order-form snippet we use for credit calculation. If that looks good we can incorporate into the MSA redline and return to you.

Proposed availability addendum (draft language):
- Availability SLA: Redwood will make the Service available 99.5% of the time in any given calendar month, measured over the calendar month, excluding defined carve-outs.
- Measurement: Availability is calculated as (TotalSeconds - UnavailableSeconds) / TotalSeconds for the calendar month.
- Credit: For each full 0.1% below the SLA, Nexus will receive a service credit equal to 5% of that month’s recurring invoice for the affected service, up to a maximum of 50% of the monthly recurring charges. Credits are Nexus’s sole and exclusive remedy for availability failures.

Carve-outs (examples):
- Scheduled maintenance (>= 30 minutes with >= 48 hours notice)
- Emergency maintenance (reasonable notice)
- Force majeure, third-party provider outages, and customer-caused issues (including excessive traffic violating published rate limits)
- Regional failover/test drills when Nexus has requested multi-region routing or has opted into cross-region replication

Order-form phrasing (sample):
- Service Tier: Hosted (Pilot) / Dedicated (Production)
- Availability SLA: 99.5% monthly (Hosted, Pilot) / 99.9% monthly (Dedicated, optional)
- Latency SLO: P95 <= 250ms (Dedicated) — measured at the Redwood ingress point for production routes in the specified region.

Operational notes:
- We measure availability at our API ingress (token acceptance + 2xx generation). Network-level issues between Nexus and our region are not included unless corroborated by Redwood traces.
- Latency measurements exclude cold-starts for ephemeral model instances and the first request after a model swap when cache warming occurs; these events will be logged and treated as maintenance if pre-notified.

I’m attaching a redline-friendly snippet and a simple credit calculation table. Marissa/Laura — any quick legal/order-form concerns before I send this back to Jordan?

— Priyom
PrIyom Das
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: PrIyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-06T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA addendum request — availability wording and credit cap

Thanks — good draft. A couple quick legal tweaks before we send to Nexus:

1) Limit credit exposure: change cap to 25% of monthly recurring charges (rather than 50%).
2) Calendar month measurement is fine; explicitly exclude partial billing periods at contract start/stop.
3) Add an escalation clause: customer must open a support ticket within 10 business days of an incident to be eligible for credit calculation.

I'll prepare tracked changes to the MSA redline if you want; otherwise Priyom you can incorporate these two points and send back. We should avoid language that implies SLA extends to 3rd-party provider availability.

Laura Bennett
Director, Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
From: PrIyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@nexushealthtech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-07T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA addendum request — availability wording and credit cap

Jordan — updated per internal feedback: attached is the revised addendum snippet and an order-form example. Key changes:

- Credit cap is 25% of monthly recurring charges (per Laura’s advice).
- Measurement is by calendar month; credits only apply if Nexus opens a support ticket within 10 business days of the incident.
- We explicitly exclude third-party provider outages from Redwood’s SLA except where Redwood controls the provider.

Attached files: SLA_Addendum_Snippet_for_Nexus.pdf, OrderForm_SLA_Table.csv

If that looks acceptable I can incorporate the wording into the MSA redline and return the final package today. Also, you mentioned model-specific latency — if you'd like, we can add a short table mapping model families to the latency objective (hosted vs dedicated).

— Priyom
From: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@nexushealthtech.com>
To: PrIyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@nexushealthtech.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-08T15:23:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA addendum request — availability wording and credit cap

Thanks, Priyom and team — the revised language looks reasonable. A couple of small asks from procurement: please add an explicit note that the SLA measurement will be the calendar month in the order form (not invoice period) and add a short clause about data residency (we require all Nexus production data to stay in us-west-2 for the pilot).

If you can add those two bullets to the final snippet and send back, procurement will route to signature. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Jordan
